items.title: Set the privacy policy build values (controller name, contact email, encarregado)
items.body:
Set the three public build values before any store submission (checklist section 1). They are baked into the bundle, never secrets:

- `VITE_PRIVACY_CONTROLLER_NAME`: the controller as published (full name, or company name and optionally CNPJ).
- `VITE_PRIVACY_CONTACT_EMAIL`: a mailbox read for privacy requests.
- `VITE_PRIVACY_DPO`: the encarregado (name and/or email; can be the owner).

Where: `deploy/homelab/.env` (production web image), the root `.env` (compose) and `code/web/.env.native.local` (native build). `missingPrivacySettings()` lists the ones still on defaults.

Raised again in the conversation of 2026-10-24 (policy is at version 3).

items.title: Controller: the owner as a natural person (CPF) or a company (CNPJ)
items.body:
The LGPD accepts both. The published name must match the developer accounts:

- Apple: an individual account publishes under the personal name; an organisation needs a D-U-N-S number.
- Google Play: a personal account created after Nov 2023 needs the closed test (12 testers, 14 days); an organisation account is exempt.

Also affects community insights (docs/design/34 O12).

items.title: Encarregado: do the small-agent rules (Res. CD/ANPD 2/2022) apply to Lotties?
items.body: Ask the lawyer whether the "agente de tratamento de pequeno porte" exemption applies, given sensitive data about children (possibly high-risk processing). If in doubt, name one (it can be the owner) in `VITE_PRIVACY_DPO`.

items.title: C1: Confirm the country and place of the home lab, and that no cloud provider stores or processes the data
items.body:
The policy says "a home lab, on their own hardware, not on a cloud provider". Affects: Who is responsible; International transfers.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C2: Confirm whether Cloudflare is DNS only or also proxies lotties.app / auth.lotties.app
items.body:
A proxy would see all traffic, including health data, and must be listed as a recipient abroad. Affects: Companies table; transfers. Note: docs/MCP.md "Known issue" also suspects a Cloudflare rule on `/.well-known/`.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C3: Confirm where PostgreSQL runs, who can reach it, and whether its disks are encrypted
items.body:
The security section claims nothing about encryption at rest; add it only if true. Affects: Security.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C4: Confirm who has administrator access to the cluster, the database, Keycloak and the logs
items.body:
The policy says access is "limited to the maintainer". Affects: Security.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C5: Confirm the Keycloak realm lotties.app settings (registration, email verification, password policy, brute force, OTP, isolation, login events)
items.body:
Registration fields, email verification, password policy, brute-force detection, OTP, isolation from other realms, login event logging (IP addresses) and its retention. Affects: What we collect; Security; Retention.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C6: Confirm whether Keycloak sends email through an SMTP relay in production
items.body:
A relay (Brevo or another) receives account email addresses and messages: it must then be added to `THIRD_PARTIES` and both tables (tests force the three to agree). Affects: Companies table.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C7: Confirm log retention (API stdout, nginx access log, Traefik access logs, Keycloak)
items.body:
The policy says "only as long as needed"; a number (e.g. 30 days) is better once confirmed. Also: are Traefik access logs on, with query strings? (gap G8). Affects: Retention.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C8: Confirm the backup routine: location, encryption, who deletes copies and when, any DB snapshots
items.body:
Besides the `pg_dump` before migration deploys. The policy says copies are deleted when no longer needed and may still hold deleted data. Affects: Retention; Security.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C9: Confirm production settings outside the repo (account deletion client, Alexa, address lookup contact, VAPID)
items.body:
`AUTH_ADMIN_CLIENT_ID/SECRET` (see the Keycloak account-deletion item), `Alexa__Enabled`, `AddressLookup__ContactEmail`, the three `PUSH_VAPID_*`. The `DRY_RUN=1` deploy plan prints whether deletion also deletes the Keycloak user. Affects: Your rights; Companies table.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C10: Enable GitHub private vulnerability reporting on the repository (or set the contact email)
items.body:
It is the default private contact of the policy; otherwise the "private report" link does not work: set `VITE_PRIVACY_CONTACT_EMAIL`. Same as audit gap G13.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C11: Confirm whether App Store Connect and Play Console share statistics and crash reports with the owner
items.body:
The policy mentions them. Affects: Companies table.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C12: Confirm the owner can answer a full access request within 15 days and erase a soft-deleted record on request
items.body:
LGPD art. 19; erasing a soft-deleted record is a manual database operation today. Affects: Your rights.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C13: Confirm significant policy changes will be announced before they apply
items.body:
There is no in-app announcement yet (gap G6). Affects: Changes.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: C14: Confirm users and the ANPD will be notified of a relevant incident (LGPD art. 48), and how
items.body:
The policy promises it. Affects: Security.

Marked `OWNER TO CONFIRM` in the audit; bring the answer to the lawyer review.

items.title: Have the privacy policy (version 3) reviewed by a Brazilian lawyer before any store submission
items.body:
The policy at `https://lotties.app/privacy` is a careful first version, not legal advice. Before App Store, Google Play or Alexa certification, a Brazilian lawyer or privacy specialist (LGPD; health data about children) should review it.

Bring: the owner checklist (C1-C14 answers), docs/design/33-privacy-audit.md, the decisions of checklist section 4, the Cry monitor microphone text (section 9) and the planned Community insights section (section 8).

items.title: Legal bases, and whether a separate stored consent for health data is needed (gap G3)
items.body: Execution of the service (art. 7, V) for the account; consent (art. 11, I) for health data; specific consent for the doctor invite; legitimate interest for logs. The app collects no separate, highlighted consent today. Decide whether that is enough or whether a consent step with a stored record is needed (Keycloak "Terms and conditions" required action, or an in-app first-run consent: an API change).

items.title: Children (LGPD art. 14): is the best-interest basis enough; must the app ask that the creator is a parent or guardian?
items.body: The policy relies on the child's best interest and the parents' use; art. 14, par. 1 asks for specific, highlighted consent of a parent or guardian. ANPD Enunciado CD/ANPD 1/2023 (as read) allows art. 7 or 11 bases when the best interest prevails. Confirm.

items.title: International transfers (art. 33): confirm art. 33, IX and whether Res. CD/ANPD 19/2024 requires more
items.body: For push services, Amazon (Alexa) and Nominatim (address lookup).

items.title: Retention periods for access log, invites, soft-deleted records, anonymized users, logs, backups
items.body: To replace "kept with the baby" and "as long as needed". Implementation follows in audit gap G4 (purge jobs).

items.title: Minimum age of account holders
items.body: The policy says the app is for adults; nothing checks it.

items.title: Wording for data about other people entered by users (doctors' contacts, the mother's RSV vaccination)
items.body: The policy makes the user responsible; confirm the wording.

items.title: Doctor's notes after removal: may a removed doctor export or delete them? (gap G10)
items.body: Today a removed doctor's notes stay with the family and she has no way to export or delete them. Decide with the lawyer (docs/design/16-doctor-access.md section 7).

items.title: G7: accept privacy#privacy-rights as Google Play's deletion URL until /delete-account exists?
items.body: Google's Data safety form asks for a public URL to request deletion. Until a public `/delete-account` page exists, decide whether `https://lotties.app/privacy#privacy-rights` (in-app steps plus the contact) is acceptable. Building the page is a separate assistant item once the text is approved.

items.title: Lawyer review of the policy's "Community insights (not active yet)" section
items.body: Both languages: whether describing a planned feature is acceptable (or better kept out until it exists), the consent wording of the future screen (design 34 section 3.5), and the honest limit of anonymisation (art. 12).

items.title: RIPD (data protection impact report) before activating community insights
items.body: Sensitive data of children, consent basis (art. 11, I and art. 14, par. 1), re-identification risk in small groups. Outline in design 34 section 8: the assistant can draft, the owner and lawyer finalize. Only before activation; nothing is built.

items.title: Legal read of the Cry monitor consent text (en + pt-BR), and whether a server-side consent record is needed
items.body:
Specific, highlighted consent of a parent or someone they allow (art. 11, I and art. 14, par. 1). Today: two checkboxes stored per device with the text version (`CRY_MONITOR_CONSENT_VERSION`). No server-side record: decide whether one is needed (an API change). Texts: `code/web/src/i18n/locales/<lang>/cryMonitor.json` `cryMonitor.consent.*`.

Policy version 3 (2026-10-24) includes the Cry monitor microphone text.

items.title: Cry monitor: may a Caregiver start it, or only a parent / legal guardian?
items.body:
Owners, Parents and Caregivers may start it today (the roles that log). Decide whether a Caregiver's "I am allowed to monitor this baby" is enough.

Policy version 3 (2026-10-24) includes the Cry monitor microphone text.

items.title: ECA Digital (Lei 15.211/2025): is a parents' app that listens in a child's room in scope?
items.body:
Sanctions from November 2026 per secondary sources. Get a legal read on scope and requirements.

Policy version 3 (2026-10-24) includes the Cry monitor microphone text.

items.title: Cry monitor: is the "inform people in the room" wording enough (nanny, domestic worker, visitors)?
items.body:
The consent and the policy tell the parent to inform anyone who may be there. Confirm, and whether more is needed for an employee.

Policy version 3 (2026-10-24) includes the Cry monitor microphone text.

items.title: Cry monitor: confirm automatic spells need no separate retention period
items.body:
They are ordinary fussy records; a "Not crying" spell is kept and marked so false alarms can be counted.

Policy version 3 (2026-10-24) includes the Cry monitor microphone text.

items.title: Confirm the "not a safety device" limits wording on the page, the consent and the policy
items.body:
"not a baby monitor and not a safety device", "can miss crying or react to other sounds", "never rely on it".

Policy version 3 (2026-10-24) includes the Cry monitor microphone text.

items.title: G3: no consent is collected or recorded for health data or children's data
items.body: Fix direction: a consent step with the policy link and a stored timestamp, or Keycloak's "Terms and conditions" required action with the policy text. Blocked on the owner/lawyer decision "Legal bases" (privacy-owner-checklist:legal-bases); then the assistant builds it.

items.title: G4: no retention limits (access log, invites, soft-deleted records, anonymized users, logs, backups)
items.body: Decide the periods (owner with the lawyer: privacy-owner-checklist:retention-periods), then the assistant adds purge jobs. Also covers the project board's own retention (soft-deleted items, revoked keys).

items.title: G6: in-app "policy updated" notice keyed on PRIVACY_POLICY_VERSION
items.body: No in-app channel announces policy changes. The policy promises it (C13) and community insights needs it before activation. Build a versioned notice keyed on `PRIVACY_POLICY_VERSION` (code/web/src/legal/privacyPolicy.ts); UI copy and placement need the owner's approval.

items.title: G8: address search text may reach proxy access logs (drop query strings of /api/v1/address/*)
items.body: The API never logs it, but Traefik's access log might. Exclude `/api/v1/address/*` or drop query strings. Needs the owner's answer to C7 (are Traefik access logs on?).

items.title: G9: nginx access log format and retention; add HSTS
items.body: The web container's nginx access log keeps client IPs and user agents; HSTS is not set. Decide log format/retention (owner) and add an HSTS middleware (deploy/homelab/README.md).

items.title: G12: docs/design/09-push-notifications.md still says "design only, nothing implemented"
items.body: Web Push is built and deployed. Fix the status line of the design doc.

items.title: Community insights O1: k: minimum distinct babies and families per cell
items.body:
Proposal: 20 babies from 20 families; p3/p97 only at 50+; hysteresis 18.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O2: Differential privacy on or off; epsilon per statistic and yearly budget
items.body:
Proposal: on, as defence in depth; weekly release at epsilon 0.2 per statistic (about 10 per statistic per year), or monthly at 0.5; chosen after the evaluation. If off, the policy's "random noise" sentence must go before activation.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O3: Final consent screen wording, and where it lives
items.body:
Proposal: design section 3.5 text; Settings > Baby; one dismissible card once. Lawyer reviews the wording.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O4: One parent's yes, or all Owners/Parents; notice to the others
items.body:
Proposal: one yes plus a notice to the others; any of them may withdraw.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O5: All-or-nothing or per-purpose consent
items.body:
Proposal: all-or-nothing in v1, `scopes` kept for later.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O6: Pooled growth statistics at all
items.body:
Proposal: not in v1; WHO curves first.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O7: Gestational age as an input (corrected age)
items.body:
Proposal: exclude preterm babies (before 37 weeks) from v1 bands instead.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O8: Retention of consent records after withdrawal or erasure
items.body:
Lawyer decides; proposal: 5 years, baby id hashed after erasure.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O9: Do doctors see the community context lines on shared sections?
items.body:
Proposal: no, until a separate review.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O10: Statistics visible to every signed-in user or only to families that opted in
items.body:
Proposal: every signed-in user (no pressure to consent).

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O11: Store label purpose: App Functionality only, or also Product Personalization
items.body:
Proposal: App Functionality.

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Community insights O12: Does the controller choice (individual or company) change anything for a pooled data set?
items.body:
E.g. a company is a better holder of consent records. Decide together with the controller question (privacy-owner-checklist:controller).

Community insights is planned, opt-in only and not built; all of O1-O11 must be taken before activation (design 34 section 12).

items.title: Try the cry monitor on a real phone (mic permission, wake lock, iOS 18.4+) and read the consent text
items.body:
Hub > App > Cry monitor on a real device: microphone permission prompt and persistence, Screen Wake Lock, an iPhone on iOS 18.4 or later, behaviour on relaunch. Read the consent and intro copy (the orchestrator's draft; the owner's read is still open, CD0).

No recorded cry through a real microphone has been verified yet (CD2 ran with a synthetic stream).

items.title: CD0: owner read of the cry monitor copy (consent, intro, limits)
items.body: CD3 shipped with the orchestrator's draft copy; the owner's read (and the legal read, privacy-owner-checklist:cry-consent-legal) is still open. Remaining CD0 scope (foreground only, zero-shot YAMNet, push default off) is decided.

items.title: CD2 follow-up: manual check with a recorded cry through a virtual microphone
items.body: The CD2 manual check ran with a synthetic oscillator stream, not a recorded cry played through a virtual microphone on Chrome desktop. Still to do.

items.title: CD8: device checklist on HTTPS (old Android, iPhone iOS 18.4+): CPU, battery, heat, wake lock, call, relaunch
items.body: Load, CPU, battery per hour, heat, Wake Lock, relaunch, a phone call, permission persistence; fixes. The owner holds the devices; the assistant prepares the checklist and fixes. iOS PWA microphone bugs (relaunch, audio route) are a known risk: test early.

items.title: CD9: pilot with consenting families (confirmed share, missed cries per device; tune sensitivity)
items.body: Assistant: pilot design (section 10: what to measure, aggregates only, consent). Owner: recruit consenting families. Adjust the sensitivity table from the results. Blocked on CD8 and on the legal read of the consent.

items.title: CD10: native background listening (Android foreground service, iOS background audio), separate go/no-go
items.body: Native capture with MediaPipe Tasks Android; iOS background audio spike. Needs store declarations: the native apps request no microphone permission today, so store labels change when this ships (checklist section 9). Blocked on CD9.

items.title: cry_detected push: deliver inside quiet hours?
items.body: As built, `cry_detected` pushes are delivered inside quiet hours (the monitor mostly runs at night, when quiet hours are on by default). An owner decision to confirm.
items.source: docs/design/31-cry-detector-spike.md notes on CD4 and CD6

items.title: Send the SBP and SBIm permission emails (docs/SBP-PERMISSION-REQUEST.md)
items.body: Review, fill in every `[...]` and send the draft. Nothing is sent by the project. Answers settle R-DOC-1 (vaccine calendars) and L1 (SBP sleep and feeding sources). Once sent, the wait is external.

items.title: R-DOC-1: vaccine data licences (gov.br CC BY-ND; SBP and SBIm all rights reserved)
items.body: Owner decision before publishing: rely on facts-only reuse with attribution, or wait for SBP/SBIm permission (emails item). Same decision as age norms L1.

items.title: L1: SBP sleep and feeding sources are "all rights reserved"
items.body: `sbp-sono-2025`, `sbp-alimentacao-2024`: no reuse licence. Rely on facts-only reuse with attribution, or ask SBP (same open decision as R-DOC-1).

items.title: L2: read the Ministry of Health feeding guide's licence line (Guia alimentar 2019)
items.body: The copyright page's licence line could not be read from the PDF text. If it is a non-commercial or share-alike Creative Commons licence it governs the document; Lotties reuses facts only (meal counts). Owner to confirm from the printed or rendered page.

items.title: L3: re-check the NSF "may be appropriate" sleep ranges against the journal article
items.body: They were read from a reprint (the journal table answered HTTP 403); recommended ranges were confirmed on thensf.org.

items.title: L5 / R-AN-4: read the 2023 WHO complementary feeding guideline and cite it
items.body: The 2011 Q&A page was used; the 2023 guideline (usually CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO) would be the better citation.

items.title: R-AN-5: re-check Ministry of Health Caderno de Atencao Basica 23 (it answered HTTP 503)
items.body: It may give Brazilian feed counts and diaper signs. Also R-AN-2: confirm the guide's page numbers (pp. 117-127, 148-151) against the printed guide.

items.title: Bottle chips: move the cold-start ranges (months 0-3) to the published SBP/AAP union?
items.body: The published Brazilian table (SBP) is consistently above the app's rows 0-3. The chips are shortcuts, never targets; the owner decides whether to move them.

items.title: R-DOC-2: re-download the SBP vaccine calendar PDF and compare before release
items.body: The PDF link carries a nonce; the file was modified on 2026-09-10, after its printed date (2026-07-28).

items.title: R-DOC-4/5/6: PNI calendar changes to watch (PCV20 switch, revised technical calendar, IN CNV 2026)
items.body: P3 (2026-01-30) predates PCV20 and the VIP 2nd booster; PCV10 at 4 months moves to PCV20 at 2, 4 and 12 months when stocks end; the Instrucao Normativa CNV 2026 was not read. Re-check and update the schedule file (yearly update procedure: docs/design/18 section 8).

items.title: R-DOC-7: SBIm adolescent (10-19 years) recommendations are absent
items.body: SBIm values stop below 10 years; SBIm-only adolescent doses may be missing.

items.title: Run the ANVISA CatalogImporter against production (dry run first) for curated products and strengths
items.body:
Applies the curated products and the structured strengths (production shows "strength not known" until it runs) and the Flygas -> Fly Gotas alias merge. Dry run first, then the real run. Agents never run it against the real database (CLAUDE.md).

Tool: `code/api/tools/Lotties.CatalogImporter` (docs/design/13-anvisa-catalog.md).

items.title: Rename the owner's own "Flygass" medication to Fly Gotas
items.body: "Flygass" is the owner's own medication entry (not a catalog product). After the importer run, rename it in the app.

items.title: Pharmacist review of the curated list (ingredients, age suitability, warnings, equivalence labels)
Fly Gotas 150: still notified and sold under that name; is it suitable at this concentration for babies?
items.body: Official data only has inactive notified records. Also: is listing it with Luftal (75 mg/mL) as "same ingredient, different strength" enough?

items.title: Luftal: registration inactive: still sold, and in which formulation (75 mg/mL)?
items.body: CMED still lists presentations.

items.title: Colidis: should the app show any of the manufacturer's claims (age, colic relief)?
items.body: Confirmed by packaging as a food supplement (L. reuteri DSM 17938); claims are unchecked. Is "same ingredient" meaningful for probiotic strains?

items.title: Sorine and Rinosoro saline entries: confirm sodium chloride and concentration from the box
items.body: The notified products list no ingredient; these entries deliberately state no concentration (0.9 % vs hypertonic).

items.title: Apple Developer Program membership approval (pending at Apple)
items.body: Applied; waiting for Apple. Then: App ID `app.lotties.app`, the App Store Connect app record, the App Store Connect API key and the four iOS secrets, and the first TestFlight run (separate items).

items.title: iOS: register the App ID app.lotties.app and create the App Store Connect app
items.body: developer.apple.com > Identifiers > App IDs: Bundle ID (explicit) `app.lotties.app`, no capabilities now (Push Notifications later, native push). appstoreconnect.apple.com > New App: iOS, name Lotties (have a fallback), bundle `app.lotties.app`, SKU `lotties-ios`. Then App Information (category, age rating, privacy URL, App Privacy answers). Blocked on the membership approval.

items.title: iOS: create the App Store Connect API key (Admin) and set ASC_KEY_ID, ASC_ISSUER_ID, ASC_KEY_P8, APPLE_TEAM_ID
items.body: Users and Access > Integrations > App Store Connect API > Team Keys > Generate, access Admin (cloud signing creates certificates). The `.p8` downloads once. Secrets go only into GitHub Actions secrets, never the repo or `.env`. Blocked on the membership approval.

items.title: iOS: first workflow run with upload to TestFlight; fix the first-run failures
items.body: Run Mobile release (ios only, `upload_testflight`). The workflow has never run: expect signing fixes (the log names the missing piece). The owner starts the run; the assistant fixes the workflow.

items.title: Set the repository variable LOTTIES_OIDC_CLIENT_ID (public client id) for the mobile workflow
items.body: Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables. The same value as the web build's `VITE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` (public, not a secret).

items.title: Android: create the upload keystore and set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 and the three keystore secrets
items.body: `keytool -genkeypair ... -alias upload` then base64 on one line; keep the file and passwords in a password manager. Secrets: `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS`, `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` (GitHub Actions secrets only).

items.title: Android: create the Play Console app and upload the first AAB by hand (internal testing)
items.body: Play Console > Create app (Lotties, App, Free). Run the workflow (android only, no upload), download the AAB, Internal testing > accept Play App Signing > upload > roll out. Fill App content (privacy URL, ads none, app access with demo login, audience adults, Data safety, health declaration) and the store listing. Google requires the first AAB by hand.

items.title: Android: closed test with 12 testers opted in for 14 days in a row (personal account rule)
items.body: A personal developer account created after Nov 2023 cannot publish to production before this. Invite 12 people (each needs a Google account), keep them opted in 14 days, then apply for production access. Internal testing does not count. An organisation account is exempt (controller decision). Confirm the current rule in the console.

items.title: Android: PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON for automatic Play uploads (after the first manual AAB)
items.body: Only then set the secret and use the `upload_play` input or a tag. The service account needs release permissions for this app only.

items.title: The mobile release workflow has never run (expect first-run fixes)
items.body: Validated only as YAML and by reading. Unverified: the auto-created `App` scheme, JDK 21 for Capacitor, Apple API key flags for archive/export on macos-26 with Xcode 26.5, the TestFlight upload through `destination=upload`.

items.title: CLA or contribution clause in CONTRIBUTING (AGPL code in the app stores)
items.body: The owner can publish their own code; outside contributions need a grant to ship through the stores. Options: CLA / DCO plus a clause, dual licence, or no outside code in the app. A draft clause is in section 9 (a legal change: owner to approve; confirm with a lawyer).

items.title: Public /delete-account page for Google Play's deletion URL
items.body: Public page explaining the in-app path (Settings > Account and data), what is deleted and what stays, and a contact for people who cannot sign in; landing footer link. Waits on the owner approving the text (and the G7 decision).

items.title: Keycloak and API for the native apps: redirect URIs, web origins, CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
items.body: Before testers sign in from the native apps: the app redirect (`app.lotties.app://auth`) and origins `https://localhost`, `capacitor://localhost` (docs/design/12 sections 4 and 5).

items.title: Store forms: App Privacy, Data safety, age/content rating, health declaration
items.body: Answers are drafted in section 3 (checked against the privacy audit), 6 and 7; the owner fills the consoles and confirms the "owner to confirm" answers (Apple analytics, Alexa transfer).

items.title: Store listing and review notes: descriptions, screenshots (en, pt-BR), support URL, demo accounts
items.body: No medical claims; credits and privacy URLs in the description. Review notes: a dedicated demo user with synthetic events for a fake baby and a second demo user for sharing (never real credentials in the repo). The assistant drafts text and screenshots; the owner creates accounts and submits.

items.title: Native push (APNs/FCM) and isNativeApp() in the notification settings before the first iOS review
items.body: docs/design/19-native-push.md is design only; needs vendor accounts (Apple Developer Program, Firebase project). The server side can be written against fake HTTP handlers first.

items.title: Fix the /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource routing (Traefik/Cloudflare sends it to the web app) BEFORE enabling MCP
items.body:
The Ingress routes the path to `lotties-api`, but through Traefik and Cloudflare a request is answered by the web service (HTML, 200). `/api/...` and the API pod directly answer correctly. No other Ingress claims the path.

Try: Traefik router priority for the path (a separate Ingress with `traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.priority`), whether Traefik reloaded its config, any Cloudflare rule on `/.well-known/`. Check: `curl -i https://lotties.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` returns JSON, not HTML. Cluster changes need the owner's go-ahead.

items.title: MCP: Keycloak client scopes lotties.read / lotties.write with the audience mapper and consent texts
items.body: Two optional client scopes with consent texts (en, pt-BR realm overrides) and an Audience mapper `https://lotties.app/api/v1/mcp` (never `lotties-api`). Short access tokens (5 min), refresh token rotation.

items.title: Enable the project board: Keycloak realm roles, Board__Enabled, Board__Mcp__Enabled, first API key
items.body:
1. Realm `lotties.app`: create `lotties-board-reader`, `-writer`, `-admin`; check the `realm_access.roles` mapper; assign `lotties-board-admin` to the owner (docs/KEYCLOAK-BOARD.md sections 2-4).
2. `Board__Enabled: "true"` and `Board__Mcp__Enabled: "true"` under `env:` in `deploy/homelab/values/api.yaml`, own commit, deploy (migration `ProjectBoard` first).
3. Create the first write API key (expiry set) for Claude Code; keep it in `LOTTIES_BOARD_KEY` on that machine.
4. Import this seed: `node scripts/board-import.mjs --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run`.

items.title: pg_dump backup only before deploys that apply a migration

items.decisionSummary: One Application layer of assistant commands with two adapters (Alexa endpoint, MCP server). Never medication doses or advice through any assistant. MCP read-only by default, writes opt-in; both off until enabled.
items.rationale: One set of rules and tests for both assistants; dose errors by voice are a safety risk.

items.title: Cry detector: detection, not cause; zero-shot YAMNet; foreground monitor only
items.body: Detect sustained crying on the device (YAMNet via MediaPipe, zero-shot, no training of ours) in a foreground monitor mode; nothing recorded or sent; not a safety device. Audio cause classification rejected.
items.decisionSummary: Detect sustained crying on the device (YAMNet via MediaPipe, zero-shot, no training of ours) in a foreground monitor mode; nothing recorded or sent; not a safety device. Audio cause classification rejected.
items.rationale: Cause classification has weak accuracy and false-reassurance risk; on-device detection keeps audio private.

items.title: Deploy procedure: only from the normal clone, clean tree on main, in WSL
items.body:
- Deploy ONLY from the main clone with a clean tree on `main` (the owner's two local `.gitignore` lines aside): `DRY_RUN=1 ./deploy/homelab/deploy.sh`, then `./deploy/homelab/deploy.sh`.
- Never from a git worktree: WSL cannot read a Windows worktree's `.git` file (image tags collapsed once and a stale image was reused; `deploy.sh` now refuses).
- The owner's two local `.gitignore` lines (`CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/`) must stay out of every commit.
- Integrate and deploy one feature at a time, in the order they finish (docs/PROCESS.md).
- Back up the database only before a deploy that applies a migration; apply migrations first.

items.title: Migrations: regen undeployed ones, pin deployed ones after each deploy
items.body:
- `scripts/regen-migrations.sh <Name>` re-creates a migration that was never applied to any database (it refuses deployed ones).
- After each deploy that shipped a migration, built-in event type or notification kind, pin it: `DeployedMigrations` in `MigrationTests.cs`, `DeployedKeys` in `BuiltInEventTypesTests.cs`, codes in `NotificationValueObjectTests.cs` (a small commit on main; workers never edit these lists).
- Code-first EF only; `dotnet ef migrations add`; never commit a SQL script.

items.title: Hygiene: no leftover processes; only br-* containers; flaky tests
items.body:
- No leftover workers, dev servers, containers or launchers after a task; check for runaway CPU processes (a stray loop once made tests flaky all night).
- Containers: Podman in WSL. Never stop, remove or prune anything not named `br-*`; own names and high ports only; `--network host`.
- Known flaky tests: timing-sensitive web tests under CPU load (e.g. `coldStart.test.tsx` B1, fixed by REVIEW #21). Re-run once before chasing; record new ones here.
- Never read, print or commit the root `.env`; secrets live only there and in the owner's deploy `.env`.

items.title: Owner preferences: terse replies, own UI, one worktree per worker
items.body:
- Terse replies.
- The UI must not copy Napper.
- Deploy each worker's result as soon as it finishes, one git worktree per worker.
- All AI-produced docs under `docs/`; agent-only files in `docs/agents/`.
- Subagents: Opus plans/orchestrates, Sonnet medium-hard, Haiku simple, never Fable.

items.title: Infrastructure map (no secrets)
items.body:
- Home lab Kubernetes, kubectl context `home-lab-main`; app namespace `lotties-app-production`.
- Images in the owner's Harbor registry; deploy kit `deploy/homelab` (Helm releases `lotties-api`, `lotties-web`).
- Keycloak realm `lotties.app` at `https://auth.lotties.app` (shared Keycloak, single replica: test before touching it).
- Ingress class `traefik-external`; Cloudflare in front (DNS; proxying to be confirmed, C2). Public host `https://lotties.app` (`/api` to the API).
- PostgreSQL outside the cluster; the API uses a role limited to DML; migrations by the migrator role.
- Any cluster change needs the owner's explicit go-ahead; read-only kubectl is fine.

items.title: Known load-flaky web tests (pass alone)
items.body: When the full vitest run fails, re-run the failing files ALONE before treating it as a regression. Known load-flaky (they pass alone): EventSheet (reduced motion), SettingsPage (creates a custom type), DoctorInbox (accepting), IllustrationGallery, LandingPage, PrescriptionSheet, ProposalSheet, CreditsPage, SettingsPage.moved. Also common: `DatabaseClosedError` unhandled rejections from AppShell/NowScreen/HubScreen tests under load (they also happen on base commits). After a merge also clear `code/web/.vite-cache` if the catalog test fails oddly.
